matches.rationale: GT 1 describes mathematically invalid concatenation notation and index misalignment in Equation (3)'s derivation. Pred 10 identifies a dimensional inconsistency in Equation (2) regarding summation of different-sized token blocks. These are related but distinct issues in adjacent equations; pred 10 does not address the concatenation-inside-matrix-multiplication or semicolon notation problems specific to Eq (3).

GT 2 identifies incorrect attention scaling by sqrt(N_t) (token count) instead of sqrt(d) (embedding dimension) in Equations (5)-(6). Pred 6 directly captures this same issue, noting the inconsistency between main text using sqrt(d) and Appendix using sqrt(N_t) for the identical cross-attention operation, and explains that d and N_t are different quantities.

GT 3 concerns the frozen visual connector in Qwen2.5-VL creating an unfair experimental comparison bias. Pred 4 and 7 mention the Qwen2.5-VL connector claim but focus on unsupported performance claims and orphaned text fragments, not the experimental design asymmetry or fairness issue that GT 3 identifies.

GT 4 identifies MME values above 900-1000 in Table 2 as severely misscaled compared to literature (which reports <100). Pred 1 directly captures this, noting the LLaMA2 LoRA MME value of 90.85 in Table 2 is inconsistent with 908.52 reported elsewhere, and that all other Table 2 MME values lie in the 774-1025 range, confirming the scale mismatch.

GT 5 identifies overgeneralized claims of 'consistent improvements' in the abstract that conflict with heterogeneous experimental outcomes. Pred 2 captures the abstract's hedging contradicted by Section 6's absolute claims; pred 4 and 5 document specific instances where claimed superiority is unsupported by Table 1 and Table 3 data, collectively demonstrating the claim-evidence mismatch GT 5 describes.

GT 6 concerns removal or weakening of the Broader Impacts ethical discussion in the Appendix. None of the findings address ethical content, transparency, or broader impacts sections; all findings focus on technical, mathematical, or data consistency issues.

GT 7 identifies inflated rhetoric in the conclusion claiming MokA as a definitive advance while also calling it 'preliminary,' creating misleading impressions. Pred 2 directly captures this contradiction, noting the abstract's hedging ('gains vary...further exploration needed') versus Section 6's absolute language ('completely solves...groundbreaking...final, conclusive'), which is the same rhetorical manipulation GT 7 describes.

GT 8 identifies baseline methods occasionally outperforming MokA in Table 3, contradicting universal superiority claims. Pred 3 documents Multiple LoRA vs MokA inconsistencies across Tables 3 and 5; pred 13 notes Cross-attention* data anomalies; pred 15 captures the Gate variant ranking reversal where it underperforms in Table 3 but outperforms elsewhere—all demonstrating the selective reporting and contradictory data GT 8 describes.

GT 9 concerns fabricated or premature references [1], [2], [35] with suspicious arXiv IDs and promotional titles. None of the findings examine reference integrity, citation validity, or bibliographic fabrication; all focus on internal paper content.

GT 10 identifies a global narrative inconsistency: Introduction claims equal importance of cross-modal adaptation, yet partial modality experiments show text dominates, undermining the balanced adaptation rationale. While pred 5 notes claim-evidence mismatches, none of the findings specifically address the Introduction's partial modality inference experiments or the text-dominance contradiction GT 10 describes.

GT 11 concerns the partial modality inference protocol artificially disabling cross-attention and biasing evaluation against non-text modalities. None of the findings discuss the experimental protocol for partial modality inference, cross-attention disabling during inference, or the resulting evaluation bias.

GT 12 identifies inflated marketing-like language in the Related Work section overstating MokA as a 'targeted solution' and 'definitive breakthrough.' Pred 2 addresses similar rhetoric but in the abstract and conclusion, not the Related Work section; the specific location and context differ.

GT 13 identifies Table 6 reporting 1.069× forward time while Appendix tables show up to 13.4% and 21.3% increases, understating computational cost. Pred 12 directly captures this, noting Table 6's 1.134× value matches the three-modality AVL setting from Appendix D rather than the two-modality setting implied by POPE, demonstrating the misrepresentation of overhead GT 13 describes.

GT 14 concerns inconsistency in Section 4.4's description of cross-attention variants: original MokA keeps text unchanged while cross-attention* updates text, but this reversal is unexplained. Pred 13 notes data anomalies in the Cross-attention* row but does not address the mechanism description inconsistency or query/key role reversal that GT 14 identifies.

GT 15 identifies notation inconsistency in Equation (13) where the cross-modal text term is written as a zero vector without matrix B, breaking uniform application of projection. Pred 11 directly captures this, noting 'B * 0_{N_t}' has dimensional mismatch (B is d×r, 0_{N_t} is length N_t) and should be the zero matrix 0_{d×N_t} for consistent block concatenation.
